title: Offline separation and source roles
contract: The manual describes separation inside Live without Internet or additional external tools, for mono/stereo recorded audio. This is an offline-workflow claim, not a requirement to reproduce the named private deep-learning mechanism or accept every file/container. Existing media owners retain import/decode eligibility.

title: Command entry and options dialog
contract: Separate Stems to New Audio Tracks is documented in context/Create menus for Browser audio files and Session/Arrangement audio clips; invoking it opens the separation options dialog. Exact unsupported input, command enablement and platform shortcut behavior remain unknown.

title: Element selection
contract: Vocals, Drums, Bass and Others toggles choose included elements. Others denotes parts not detected as the other three. No exact classifier, perceptual-purity, reconstruction, source-isolation or stochastic-output law follows.

title: Merge selection eligibility
contract: Merge to Single Track combines selected parts and can be enabled only with two or three elements selected. With one or all four selected the checkbox cannot be activated. Zero-selected behavior, changing selection after enable and disabled-versus-hidden presentation are unknown.

title: Quality selector
contract: The dialog offers High Speed and High Quality. They represent documented speed/quality choices, without a processing-time bound, SDR threshold, universal quality ordering, model identity or output-sample oracle.

title: Separate and transport stop
contract: Separate starts the process; if playback is running it stops when separation begins. Completion latency, stop timing, recording interaction, cancellation and failure atomicity remain unknown.

title: Separate multiple-element structure and colors
contract: For multiple unmerged output elements, each resulting stem is a clip on its own track in a new Group Track. Stem track/clip colors correspond to dialog toggles; the group uses the source clip track color. Exact palette, source-less Browser color and track placement/order are unknown.

title: Single and merged output structure
contract: One separated element creates a single track/clip instead of a group. With Merge enabled the merged stem is placed on a new track whose track/clip color uses source track color. Exact input insertion position and effect/automation placement in these nongroup branches are unknown.

title: Clip region and warped-loop processing
contract: For Session/Arrangement clips, adjusted start/end markers restrict separation to the audible region. With a warped loop, the manual describes processing from the start marker through the active loop region. Exact end inclusivity, loop cycles, offset mapping, Warp rendering and sample boundaries remain unknown.

title: Arrangement time-selection command
contract: Separate Stems for Time Selection is a clip context-menu route on an Arrangement time selection and opens the same dialog. After Separate, the clip splits at selection edges and only selected audio is processed. Exact boundary rounding, overlapping clips and transaction/undo behavior remain unknown.

title: Effects and automation transfer for grouped outputs
contract: In the documented grouped-output case, source-track audio effects are added to the Group Track rather than baked into separated audio; track automation goes to the group and clip automation/modulation to individual stem clips. This is a placement role, not a rendered equivalence or device identity/deep-copy law. Single/merged nongroup target placement is unresolved.

title: Source clip deactivation
contract: After stems are created, the source clip is deactivated to prevent doubled output; selecting it and pressing 0 reactivates it. Exact key focus/layout, failed-process/cancel behavior and source-file rewriting are unknown; general clip activation remains with the editing owner.

title: Browser destination and empty-Set tempo condition
contract: Browser-source results go to Session or Arrangement according to focus. In an empty Set with warping for samples enabled in Record, Warp & Launch settings, project tempo is updated to source audio tempo. This conditional role does not define detection, empty-Set predicate, tempo estimate, beat conversion or behavior when the conditions are false.

title: Generated file destination and format roles
contract: Stem files are documented under Current Project Samples/Processed/Stems. Merge also creates individual stem files along with the merged file. Output uses Record, Warp & Launch file type,44100Hz and source bit depth according to this captured chapter. Accepted source representations, names, collisions, file codec/resampling, metadata and target output values remain unverified.

title: High Quality Others dependencies
contract: For High Quality with Others selected, all parts are processed even if only some are requested. The example Vocals+Others adds only those two to the Set, while Drums/Bass files are stored in Stems. This gives an externally documented file/Set distinction; it does not mandate private pass structure or a completion-time relation.

title: Algorithm, numerical and boundary outcomes
contract: Classifier/model output, quality/SDR/reconstruction, stochastic behavior, Warp/time/sample boundaries, accepted formats, bit-depth/file codecs and unsupported input/output remain required unknowns.

title: Single, merged and interaction gaps
contract: Effects/automation placement for nongroup branches, Browser source-less color, device identity/parameter bindings, multiple-source/track ordering, time-selection fragment activation and source preservation remain unknown.

title: Lifecycle, failure and resource outcomes
contract: Undo/redo/cancel/save, source/output loss, disk/network/build/feature availability, rate/resource limits, transport/record ordering and teardown remain required unknowns.
